lena (AM): FYI escalated from ACME, production traffic from their VPC is being routed to us-east nodes even though their infra is in us-west. High tail latency + cross-region billing.
maya (Support): Thanks — they sent a sample req_id=abc123. Zoe, can you paste the exact curl you used?
zoe (Customer): zoe: here — curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'  // response shows header Server-Region: us-east-1 and 900ms latency
ajay (SRE): quick hypothesis: their egress NAT/public IP is geolocated to us-east, our smart-router picks region by source IP. Can we confirm their outgoing IP? ask them to run: `curl -s https://ifconfig.co`
zoe (Customer): did that -> 34.201.55.12
diego (Infra): 34.201.55.12 resolves to an AWS IP range in us-east-1, yep. They said they peer to a partner who NATs traffic in another region.
maya (Support): that matches: routing is by egress IP -> then fallback policy picks closest available capacity in that region. Explains cross-region latency + token billing.
ajay (SRE): repro steps I ran from our lab: `traceroute api.redwood.ai` from an endpoint with an us-east egress IP returns hops into us-east transit, then us-east edge. If we force egress from a us-west IP it hits us-west.
nick (Platform-bot): Note: on private deployments customers can configure `egress_ip_allowlist` and `preferred_region` in the control plane. If not set, region selection falls back to geolocation.
lena (AM): Customer swears nothing changed on their side; they are on-prem and use a central corporate NAT/HDX appliance that forwards through partner colo in us-east.
ajay (SRE): Immediate triage checklist for support -> 1) ask customer to run `curl -s https://ifconfig.co` and `dig +short myip.opendns.com @resolver1.opendns.com` 2) traceroute to api.redwood.ai 3) share req_id and timestamp so we can check routing logs.
maya (Support): Received traceroute output from them: ```traceroute to api.redwood.ai (52.2.14.8), 30 hops max 1 10.0.0.1 2 203.0.113.45 3 198.51.100.2 4 52.2.14.8``` -> intermediate ASN shows partner transit in us-east.
diego (Infra): Root cause = egress SNATed in partner region. Two remediation options: (A) customer changes egress so SNAT stays in same region (preferred), or (B) we make an exception: map customer's control-plane tenancy to prefer us-west via control-plane override (requires security review).
ajay (SRE): Short-term workaround: they can call regional endpoint directly: `https://us-west-2.api.redwood.ai/v1/...` (this bypasses region selection by source IP). Also suggest adding header `X-Redwood-Preferred-Region: us-west-2` for Private customers if control plane is configured to respect it.
zoe (Customer): Is there a configuration doc for the region override? I can ask infra to change NAT but might take weeks.
nick (Platform-bot): Linking internal doc: /docs/private/egress-and-region-mapping (internal). For this customer, we can add their egress IP 34.201.55.12 to their tenancy mapping so our router forces us-west routing. Needs ticket to Platform.
maya (Support): I'll open a Platform ticket and mark P1 for customer SLA. Also emailing them steps to test direct region endpoint.
lena (AM): Customer expects confirmation before EOD. Diego/Ajay — can Platform do a temporary mapping and whitelist?
diego (Infra): I can add a temporary mapping but need owner's OK and signed AUP. Also will add a note: long-term they should use regional NAT or site-to-site with egress in same region.
ajay (SRE): For root-cause docs: add note that corporate proxies or peering that NAT outside region will cause wrong-region selection; network teams should preserve source egress locality or use regional endpoints.
maya (Support): Action items: 1) I will send direct-region curl example and ask for egress check (done) 2) Lena to approve AUP signoff 3) Platform ticket created referencing req_id=abc123 and ip=34.201.55.12 4) Diego will apply temporary tenancy mapping once approvals are in.
lena (AM): Approved — proceed. Please post when mapping is live.
diego (Infra): mapping applied at 1763305100, routing table updated.
maya (Support): sent notice to customer and asked them to retry.
zoe (Customer): confirmed retries now show Server-Region: us-west-2 and latency down to 130ms. Thanks team :thumbsup:
ajay (SRE): Recommend follow-up: doc the egress checklist in onboarding and add automated alert that detects large fraction of tenancy traffic leaving via foreign-region IPs.
nick (Platform-bot): Logged incident and follow-up tasks in internal tracker #PLAT-449.
maya (Support): closing the escalation once customer confirms stability.
lena (AM): Great work everyone.
